name: Genetic Intestinal Disease Due to Fat Malabsorption

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Fat Malabsorption

criteria.description: Presence of chronic steatorrhea with bulky, foul-smelling stools
Laboratory evidence of fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K) deficiencies
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with fat absorption
Exclusion of pancreatic insufficiency as cause of malabsorption
Histological evidence of normal villous architecture without inflammatory changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic steatorrhea, fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies, and confirmation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes of fat malabsorption such as pancreatic insufficiency or celiac disease.

laboratory: Elevated fecal fat on quantitative stool fat analysis
Low serum levels of vitamins A, D, E, and K
imaging: Normal small bowel imaging without structural abnormalities
Bone density scans showing osteopenia or osteoporosis
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes involved in intestinal fat absorption (e.g., FATP4, SLC27A4)
other: Normal small bowel biopsy excluding villous atrophy or inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Pancreatic insufficiency with elevated sweat chloride test
Villous atrophy on small bowel biopsy

redFlags: Severe failure to thrive despite nutritional support
Recurrent bleeding episodes due to coagulopathy
Neurological deterioration including ataxia or peripheral neuropathy
